summary: Iteration 3 verified: /api/r bridge fully compensates for Telegram's 64-char /start payload cap. Extended backend_test.py from 23 → 33 tests, ALL 33 PASS. Bridge happy path: 140-char click_id → HTTP 302, Location=https://t.me/tamil_best_service_bot?start=<token>, token is 12 chars from [A-Za-z0-9_-] (charset+length hard-asserted), bot_clicks doc stored with full untruncated click_id (len match), used_at=null, created_at present. Alternate keys click_id/clickid/cid all produce mappings. Extra params (campaign, spot) land in doc.params subdoc and are NOT merged into click_id. GET /api/r with no click id → 302 https://t.me/tamil_best_service_bot (no ?start=) and creates ZERO bot_clicks. Unique index bot_clicks.token exists (idempotent in post_init). bot.resolve_click_id(token,user_id) returns EXACT full click_id string and stamps used_at + user_id; unknown payload passes through unchanged (raw click ids still work). End-to-end on_start with a bridge token in context.args: bot_events.source == FULL click_id (NOT the token) AND fire_postback is called with the FULL click_id — resolution happens BEFORE track and BEFORE postback as required. Dedupe holds on resolved id: 2 fire_postback calls → 1 bot_postbacks doc + exactly 1 outbound httpx.get. /start with no payload still tracks + replies, no postback, no bot_clicks. GET /api/bot/clicks returns ad_url ending in '/api/r?click_id={click_id}' (updated from stale iter-2 assertion), direct_bot_link='https://t.me/tamil_best_service_bot', recent[] entries where click_id_length reflects RESOLVED full id length (>64 in test). Regression: supervisor telegram_bot RUNNING, log shows 'Application started' + 'trafficstars postback: ENABLED' + no Traceback, bot.py + server.py py_compile clean, no duplicated/stray code at end of bot.py, on_start uses resolve_click_id, single inline button matches env text/url, getMyCommands empty, welcome HTML parses (sendMessage chat_id=1 → 'Chat not found'), no webhook set. Frontend: page loads, @tamil_best_service_bot, Live·polling pill, data-testid=ad-url-block shows data-testid=ad-url-value = 'https://traffic-to-account.preview.emergentagent.com/api/r?click_id={click_id}', clicking data-testid=copy-ad-url flips label to 'copied', data-testid=postback-row visible showing '0 sent · 0/19 attributed'. Cleanup verified: 0 TEST_ residue across bot_clicks/bot_postbacks/bot_events/bot_users; 19 real bot_events start docs preserved untouched. No DMs to owner/user, no getUpdates/setWebhook, throwaway click ids sent only to live tsyndicate (400 invalid clickid — expected).
critical_code_review_comments: server.py /api/r uses secrets.token_urlsafe(9) → 12 chars, well under Telegram's 64-char cap. Charset is base64url = [A-Za-z0-9_-], matching Telegram's allowed set. Fix is correct.
Legacy '/api/status' + StatusCheck CRUD in server.py is still unused for this single-purpose bot — safe to remove.
bot.py post_init creates unique indexes on bot_postbacks.click_id AND bot_clicks.token idempotently — good. Both verified present in Mongo.

rca_of_the_issue: No unresolved issues. The 127-char TrafficStars click_id vs 64-char Telegram /start limit is fully mitigated: GET /api/r stores the long id keyed by a 12-char base64url token → 302s to t.me/<bot>?start=<token> → bot.on_start looks up the token in bot_clicks and passes the FULL id to both tracking (bot_events.source) and TrafficStars postback (fire_postback URL). Verified end-to-end with 33 pytest cases + live frontend.
